title: Integral section comparison reflects localized isomorphisms
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, any scheme morphism g:S to X, a pro-etale member U over S, and arbitrary internal integral modules M,N on X. The pullbacks of M,N along U.hom followed by g are isomorphic if and only if their images under the fixed section functor [def-sfb-integral-section-action-transport], restriction along the detailed completed coefficient isomorphism [def-sfb-integral-completed-coefficient-transport], actual ringed inverse image along g, and restriction to U are isomorphic. There are no point-model witnesses or finite-presentation hypotheses in this assertion.

source.place: Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(3), scalar local models; explicit comparison of the recorded coefficient presentations in step 7 of the integral constructibility bridge.

proof.text: Lift the fixed detailed source coefficient comparison to commutative ring sheaves. Use the ring-only inverse-image coefficient theorem to obtain an isomorphism to the reconstructed internal coefficient ring with exactly the required adjunct square.

Transport the already proved internal direct-image comparison through the coefficient isomorphisms. The scalar restriction square identifies the ringed direct images. Uniqueness of left adjoints, using the canonical adjunction for actual pro-etale module inverse image, gives the global section inverse-image comparison.

For algebraic modules, compose pullbacks along g and U.hom. Use the dense equivalence between the pro-etale site of U.left and the slice at U, and its module equivalence. The slice/ordinary pullback comparison identifies inverse image along U.hom with overFunctor followed by that equivalence and restriction through its coefficient isomorphism.

Conjugate an isomorphism by the functor comparison and map it through the target equivalences. Conversely use full faithfulness of the equivalences to lift an isomorphism. Combine the global internal/algebraic comparison along U.hom followed by g with the algebraic slice comparison. This preserves the statement for arbitrary modules and empty schemes.

proof_origin.place: Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); K6 uses the direct-image square and uniqueness of left adjoints, then the existing pullback compositor and slice equivalence. No finite-quotient normalization on the target is needed.

lean.statement:
theorem integralSectionLocalIsomorphisms (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (g : S ⟶ X) (U : S.ProEt)
    (M N : AdicCompletion.Modules l E X) :
    Nonempty ((CondensedRing.upperStar (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E)
        (@CategoryStruct.comp Scheme _ ((𝟭 Scheme).obj U.left) S X U.hom g)).obj M ≅
      (CondensedRing.upperStar (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E)
        (@CategoryStruct.comp Scheme _ ((𝟭 Scheme).obj U.left) S X U.hom g)).obj N) ↔
    Nonempty ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor _ U).obj
        ((Scheme.proEtaleModuleInverseImage g
          (Scheme.pbcAdicCompletion X (Scheme.pbcIntegralDatum l E))).obj
            ((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u + 1}
              (Scheme.integralDetailedCoefficientComparison X l E).hom).obj
                ((integralSectionFunctor l E X).obj M))) ≅
      (SheafOfModules.overFunctor _ U).obj
        ((Scheme.proEtaleModuleInverseImage g
          (Scheme.pbcAdicCompletion X (Scheme.pbcIntegralDatum l E))).obj
            ((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u + 1}
              (Scheme.integralDetailedCoefficientComparison X l E).hom).obj
                ((integralSectionFunctor l E X).obj N))))
